clinician.final_diagnosis: CLC (Central Lung Carcinoma) and SVC syndrome
clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient, a 64-year-old woman with a 20-pack-year smoking history, presented with persistent cough and was diagnosed with stage IV EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with brain metastases. During treatment, she developed drug-induced interstitial pneumonia. Two weeks later, she developed prominent cervicofacial edema, erythema, and dyspnea. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe SVC stenosis consistent with SVC syndrome. Balloon dilation angiography provided only temporary symptomatic relief for a few hours, and follow-up CT showed persistent SVC constriction suggesting intractable obstruction. Immunohistochemistry staining confirmed the diagnosis of CLC and SVC syndrome as the cause of her edema and dyspnea. The patient died of respiratory failure one week after the CLC diagnosis.
